To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) expressive arts are used in psychotherapy and peace-building to support affect regulation and to foster self-awareness, (2) expressive arts are also used in these settings to facilitate social cognition, and (3) expressive arts can be used in these settings in a way that builds positive rapport and trust.
the use of expressive art in the context of therapy and peacebuilding facilitates the development of cognitive capacities.
the creation of an expressive arts niche can contribute to the development of self-awareness, social understanding, and rapport and trust among individuals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role that affectivity plays in the development of cognitive capacities and the way that affective niches support cognition.
the role of affect in shaping cognition, and with the role of cognition in shaping affect.
the role that affect plays in the development of certain cognitive skills and capacities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
affective scaffolds, expressive arts, and cognition can work together in order to create a positive environment that is conducive to the development of cognitive capacities.

the relationship between affective scaffolds and cognition is not a one-way street: affective scaffolds do not simply support the realization of affective states, but also support certain cognitive processes.
affective scaffolding can be a crucial factor in the realization of certain types of cognitive capacities, and that these capacities are not only cognitive but also affective in nature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expressive arts, in addition to their affective functions, can be seen to play a significant role in cognitive development.
the expressive arts are a means of creating an affective niche, which in turn can support cognitive processes.
the affective scaffolds that are created in expressive arts contexts support both affective and cognitive development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
affectivity and cognition are not only interdependent, but also mutually constitutive.
we need to pay more attention to the affective dimension of cognitive development, and that the expressive arts are an important resource in this regard.
the relationship between emotion and cognition is more complex than is often assumed, and that affective scaffolds are a crucial resource for cognitive development.
